Code Review by Qodo

🐞 Bugs (3) 📘 Rule violations (0) 📜 Skill insights (0)
1. Unstable probe results pass curation 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>observe() compares repeated probe results with ordinary dictionary equality, which treats JSON
>values such as 1 and 1.0 as equal. When a probe alternates between those types, curation reports
>no repeatability problem even though grading uses strict_equal() to distinguish them.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[hb/curate.py[105]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/pull/14/files#diff-2711d23a867c76bd042a1431f643cededbf0dc01abf0ed75e1a03be393104fc1R105-R105) > >```diff >+ if runs[0] != runs[1]: >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>Strict probe equality matches grading semantics and prevents nondeterministic observations from
>passing curation.
>
> > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Curation's comparison uses !=, while the grading comparison explicitly requires matching JSON
>types.
>
> > [hb/curate.py\[100-107\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/9b1a67cac6bc540785088566d6ebf047523c2bcc/hb/curate.py/#L100-L107) > [hb/grade.py\[30-51\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/9b1a67cac6bc540785088566d6ebf047523c2bcc/hb/grade.py/#L30-L51) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The repeatability check accepts probe outputs whose JSON value types change between runs because Python dictionary equality treats some different types as equal. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- hb/curate.py[100-107] > >## Recommended Fix >Use the existing `strict_equal()` comparison for the two parsed observation dictionaries, and add a test with repeated outputs that differ only by JSON numeric or boolean type. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/47c37e8a-1327-4561-845b-7ecaea98c78a?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/47c37e8a-1327-4561-845b-7ecaea98c78a)
2. Ignored artifacts can fail curation 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>_curate() runs tree_changes() on the unfiltered solution tree and checks every resulting path
>against the task's allowed paths. If checks/solution contains an ignored artifact outside those
>paths, curation rejects it even though workspace_diff() removes that artifact from the patch used
>to grade the reference solution.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[hb/curate.py[R121-124]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/pull/14/files#diff-2711d23a867c76bd042a1431f643cededbf0dc01abf0ed75e1a03be393104fc1R121-R124) > >```diff >+ changed = tree_changes(pristine, solved) >+ if not changed: >+ problems.append("the reference solution changes nothing") >+ outside = out_of_scope(changed, task["scope"]["allowed_paths"]) >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>Curation should apply the same ignored-file filtering as grading to avoid false out-of-scope
>failures.
>
> > [PR-#8](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/pull/8) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Curation checks unfiltered tree changes, whereas patch construction materializes both trees with
>ignore_paths and drops matching files.
>
> > [hb/curate.py\[118-135\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/9b1a67cac6bc540785088566d6ebf047523c2bcc/hb/curate.py/#L118-L135) > [hb/patch.py\[32-40\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/9b1a67cac6bc540785088566d6ebf047523c2bcc/hb/patch.py/#L32-L40) > [hb/tree.py\[46-54\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/9b1a67cac6bc540785088566d6ebf047523c2bcc/hb/tree.py/#L46-L54) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Curation counts ignored files in its solution-change and scope checks, but the graded workspace patch excludes them. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- hb/curate.py[118-130] > >## Recommended Fix >Calculate solution changes from trees materialized with the suite's ignore rules, matching `workspace_diff()` and grading. Add a test with an ignored cache artifact outside the task's allowed paths. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/aff2d514-e0a2-4a5b-b0ca-9782eef3bcb5?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/aff2d514-e0a2-4a5b-b0ca-9782eef3bcb5)

3. A bad solution file crashes the whole suite check 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability
>
>Description >
> >
>_curate lays the reference solution over the pristine tree with a plain `shutil.copytree(solution,
>solved, dirs_exist_ok=True), which follows symlinks and copies __pycache__` and other ignored
>files. Unlike materialize, it does not drop non-regular entries. A dangling or looping symlink in
>checks/solution raises shutil.Error/OSError. curate_task only catches _Unfit and
>scripts/suite.py only catches DockerError, so one bad task aborts the check with a traceback and
>no other task gets reported.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[hb/curate.py[R118-121]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/pull/14/files#diff-2711d23a867c76bd042a1431f643cededbf0dc01abf0ed75e1a03be393104fc1R118-R121) > >```diff >+ solved = workdir / "solved" >+ shutil.copytree(pristine, solved) >+ shutil.copytree(solution, solved, dirs_exist_ok=True) >+ changed = tree_changes(pristine, solved) >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>Unfiltered copytree can abort the suite on malformed solution entries, violating per-task curation
>reliability.
>
> > [PR-#8](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/pull/8) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>curate_task only turns _Unfit into a reported problem. The overlay uses copytree with its
>default symlinks=False, so it follows symlinks, and it does not apply ignore_paths. By contrast,
>materialize skips symlinks and ignored files. The CLI catches only DockerError around
>curate_suite, so any other exception escapes.
>
> > [hb/curate.py\[50-62\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/9b1a67cac6bc540785088566d6ebf047523c2bcc/hb/curate.py/#L50-L62) > [hb/curate.py\[118-121\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/9b1a67cac6bc540785088566d6ebf047523c2bcc/hb/curate.py/#L118-L121) > [hb/tree.py\[52-88\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/9b1a67cac6bc540785088566d6ebf047523c2bcc/hb/tree.py/#L52-L88) > [scripts/suite.py\[64-68\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/harness-bench/blob/9b1a67cac6bc540785088566d6ebf047523c2bcc/scripts/suite.py/#L64-L68) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The reference solution is copied with `shutil.copytree`, which follows symlinks and copies ignored files. A broken symlink raises an exception that `curate_task` does not catch, so the whole `scripts/suite.py check` aborts. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- hb/curate.py[118-121] >- hb/curate.py[50-62] > >## Recommended Fix >Materialize the solution first with `materialize(solution, workdir / "solution", ignore)`. If it returns any dropped entries, append them as a problem, for example "checks/solution holds non-regular files: ...". Then overlay that materialized copy with `copytree(..., dirs_exist_ok=True)`. Also wrap the overlay in `try/except (OSError, shutil.Error)` and raise `_Unfit` with the message, so the failure is reported against this task instead of crashing the run. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
